clue.text: English girl after fine felt hat

indicators.note: the girl's name follows the letter from fine, so it is placed later in the answer

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An English girl comes after a fine, apparently over a hat made of felt.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft brimmed hat traditionally made of felt, so the felt hat is an example.

clue.text: Peer in uniform

definitions.meaning: a peer is someone of the same standing as another, a match
uniform here means even, the same throughout

explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a person of equal rank, and things that are uniform are even or matching throughout.

clue.text: Clothing supplier elsewhere more suitable

parts.note: someone who is out is not here, so elsewhere
fitter is the comparative of fit, meaning suitable

explanation.surface: A clothes merchant somewhere else is a better match.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shop or trader selling clothing and equipment, a supplier of garments.

clue.text: Regular publication by university breaking record

indicators.note: the university letter breaks into the record, splitting it open

parts.note: an annal is a yearly historical record

explanation.surface: A yearly publication coming from a university breaks some record.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearbook issued once a year is a regularly appearing publication.

clue.text: Choose randomly from all the players, a great many

parts.note: the cast is the full set of actors in a production
lots means a great many

explanation.surface: Someone picks at random from an entire large cast of players.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing lots is the traditional way of deciding something by chance, an idiom for a random choice.

clue.text: Servant preached, possibly giving one this?

definitions.text: Servant preached, possibly giving one this?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of servant preached are one possible rearrangement

explanation.surface: A servant gave a sermon, perhaps quoting scripture with precise references.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a preacher cites exact biblical references, giving the listener the book's section and line.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a precise reference to an authority, originally a scriptural citation as a preacher would give.

clue.text: Son leaving out du Maurier character

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of leaving are put out of order

explanation.surface: A son walks out on a figure from a du Maurier novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'out' rearranges LEAVING into VENGALI. George du Maurier wrote Trilby, whose hypnotist villain is the character.
explanation.definitionFit: The sinister hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby, whose name now means a manipulative mentor.

clue.text: Shelf where there's incomplete book of accounts

indicators.note: incomplete means the account book loses its final letter

parts.note: a ledger is a book recording accounts

explanation.surface: A shelf holds a partly finished book of accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomplete' drops the last letter R from LEDGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow flat projection, a natural shelf on a wall or cliff.

clue.text: Try to land

definitions.meaning: in rugby a try is the score made by grounding the ball over the line
to land is to come down to earth, as an aircraft does

explanation.definitionFit: In rugby and American football the grounding score is so called, and an aircraft's arrival on the runway is also called this.

clue.text: Arrived a short time ago with patient, as a precaution

parts.note: someone who has just come in arrived a short time ago
a doctor's case is a patient being treated

explanation.surface: A newcomer turns up with a patient, taking care in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing something to be ready should a problem arise, a precaution.

clue.text: Departs with peculiar revolving cylinder

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
rum is informal British for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: Someone leaves with a strange spinning cylinder.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum in machinery is a cylinder that rotates, as in a washing machine or winch.

clue.text: One inhibited by noisy petitioner

indicators.note: being held in by something, the numeral sits inside the noisy word

parts.note: clamant means loud and insistent
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is held back by a loud person making a petition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who makes a formal claim or request is a petitioner.

clue.text: German writer leaves short article

indicators.note: short means the verb for leaves loses its last letter

parts.note: goes means leaves or departs
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A German author departs, leaving behind a brief article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts the final S from GOES.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Faust is the most celebrated writer in the German language.

clue.text: Strength of character seen in 'Educating Rita'

indicators.note: seen in says the letters can be spotted within the play's title

explanation.surface: The heroine of the play Educating Rita shows real determination.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a Willy Russell play and film about a hairdresser studying literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is courage and resolve, a synonym for strength of character.

clue.text: Castles surrounding lake where birds nest

indicators.note: the chess pieces go around the lake, holding it inside

parts.note: rooks are castles in chess
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Castles beside a lake give nesting places for birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rookeries are colonies of nesting rooks or seabirds, so they are where birds nest.

clue.text: Granddaughter, perhaps, beginning to read? Joy

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of read

parts.note: elation is great joy

explanation.surface: A granddaughter starting to read brings delight.
explanation.definitionFit: A granddaughter is one example of a family member or kin.

clue.text: Programme I came across in piece of furniture

indicators.note: in places the pronoun and verb inside the piece of furniture

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture
met means came across or encountered

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled on a schedule lying on a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable is a schedule or programme of events and times.

clue.text: Hot part of Europe, including Northern Ireland once?

parts.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot

indicators.note: the European peninsula includes the letter for Northern inside it

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A warm part of Europe, perhaps once including Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern Ireland' looks like one phrase, but 'Northern' is wordplay and 'Ireland once' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romans' Latin name for the island of Ireland, now poetic or historical.

clue.text: Cicero, unexpectedly concerned with government by force

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the Roman orator's name scrambled

parts.note: on means about or concerned with

explanation.surface: The Roman statesman Cicero is surprisingly worried about rule by force.
explanation.definitionFit: Coercion is compelling people by threats or force, a description of rule through force.

clue.text: Cross about new flirtatious woman

indicators.note: about means the crossing word goes round the letter for new

parts.note: to mix breeds is to cross them

explanation.surface: Someone is angry about a new flirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is an impudent, playfully flirtatious girl or woman.

clue.text: Capone has greatest following? Not quite

indicators.note: following puts the word for greatest after the gangster's first name

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster
most means greatest in amount

explanation.surface: Does Al Capone have the biggest gang following? Not entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost means nearly but not fully, the same as not quite.

clue.text: Provoke pointer

definitions.meaning: a pointer is the indicator on a dial or compass

explanation.definitionFit: To goad someone is to needle them, and the moving arm on a gauge or compass is a needle.

clue.text: Holiday home in Grenada, charming

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words Grenada, charming

explanation.surface: A holiday home on the Caribbean island of Grenada is charming.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house, typically a summer or holiday retreat.

clue.text: Explosive article penned by unbalanced evil lot

indicators.note: penned by means the article is enclosed by the rearranged letters
unbalanced signals the letters of evil lot are disordered

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An inflammatory article is written by a deranged bunch of wrongdoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unbalanced' turns EVIL LOT into VOLTILE, and 'penned by' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatile means liable to erupt suddenly, a synonym for explosive in temper or chemistry.

clue.text: Smallest tail of mice put in at the end

indicators.note: put in means the chosen letter goes inside the word for at the end

parts.note: last means at the end

indicators.note: tail of picks the final letter of mice

explanation.surface: The tiniest mouse's tail is tucked in finally.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, meaning the smallest amount or size.

clue.text: Element unknown in Cape

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: An unidentified element is found in the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but here it supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a metallic chemical element, number 30.

clue.text: A brown rat scuttled across old vessel

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go across the letter for old, enclosing it
scuttled signals the letters of a brown rat scurry into a new order

explanation.surface: A brown rat runs across an old ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scuttled' rearranges A BROWN RAT, and 'across' puts O inside. Scuttled also hints at sinking a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrowboat is a long thin canal boat, a type of vessel.

clue.text: Commercial during flight conveys adventure

indicators.note: during puts the advertisement within the word for flight

parts.note: to take flight is to escape
an ad is a commercial advertisement

explanation.surface: An advert shown on a plane sells an exciting trip.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous adventure.

clue.text: Deal with adversary, ultimately making pact

parts.note: to treat a matter is to deal with it

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of adversary

explanation.surface: Negotiating with an enemy finally produces an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between nations, a pact.
